name: Canada
note: Canadian additions to the ITU Region 2 plan - only the allocations that genuinely differ from Region 2 or from the United States are listed here; everything else comes from the base plan. Sources, all primary: ISED RBR-4 Issue 3 (July 2022) Schedule I and its footnotes C6, C11 and C21, https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/spectrum-management-telecommunications/sites/default/files/attachments/2022/RBR-4-i3-2022-07EN.pdf (amateur bands); the machine-readable Canadian Table of Frequency Allocations, https://ised-isde.canada.ca/sat-oas/en/lists/ctfa.csv; ISED RIC-18 General Radio Service and RSS-236 (Canadian CB); ISED RSS-210 Issue 11 (2024) Annex E Table E1 and Spectrum Utilization Policy SP 462/467 MHz (licence-exempt FRS/GMRS); ISED RBR-2 Issue 1 Schedule I (marine VHF channels); and Environment and Climate Change Canada's Weatheradio Canada page. Notable Canadian differences: 70 cm is 430-450 MHz, not the US 420-450; the 1.25 m band keeps 220-222 MHz (disaster relief only) and 219-220 MHz (secondary) alongside 222-225 MHz; 60 m is the WRC-15 band 5351.5-5366.5 kHz PLUS four channels at 5332, 5348, 5373 and 5405 kHz - Canada has no 5358.5 kHz channel, unlike the US; FRS/GMRS is licence-exempt but the eight 467 MHz repeater-input channels were withdrawn, so only the seven 467 MHz interstitial channels remain; and Canada has no MURS (deferred by ISED bulletin SAB-002-14). Channel groups (the General Radio Service, FRS/GMRS, Weatheradio) are drawn from the lowest to the highest channel CENTRE frequency, so the outermost half channel falls outside the block and a block spans the gaps between its channels; single channels (the four 60 m channels, marine 21B and 83B) are drawn at their centre plus and minus half the authorised bandwidth. ISED RIC-18 states the General Radio Service band itself as 26.960 to 27.410 MHz; the block here is the 26.965 to 27.405 MHz span of its forty channel centres. INFORMATIONAL ONLY - a display aid, not an authoritative or licensing reference. JSON has no comment syntax, so this note lives in the data; the loader ignores unknown keys.
